story.headline: New rules reported for domestic LPG cylinder booking; details unconfirmed
story.body:
News18 Hindi reported on September 9 that new rules have come into force covering the booking of domestic LPG cylinders, and advised consumers to check the requirements or risk not receiving a cylinder.

The intake note received on this desk carries the same broad claim — that the government has notified new booking rules and that consumers should verify what is now required to avoid problems getting a refill.

Beyond that, the specifics are not established. The wire item seen so far does not spell out, in anything this desk can verify, which ministry or oil marketing company issued the change, what the new requirement actually consists of, or from what date it applies.

It is also not confirmed whether the rules apply to all domestic LPG consumers nationwide or only to a subset — for example subsidised connections, particular distributors or particular states. No consumer numbers, penalty provisions or official quotes are available from the material at hand.

Before this runs, the desk needs to confirm the following from primary sources: the text or press release of the notification itself and the issuing authority; the exact new requirement placed on consumers; the effective date; the scope of who is covered; and on-record comment from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or the relevant oil marketing companies. Nothing above should be published as fact on the strength of the single wire item alone.
